Markdown editor · 2026

Quill

A Markdown editor that keeps every version, offline.

Built with
TypeScript, a CRDT, IndexedDB
Status
Open source, about 2,400 people use it daily

What it is

Quill is a plain Markdown editor for people who write long things - theses, books, documentation. It saves every keystroke as history, so there is no Save button and no file you can lose.

How it works

The document is a CRDT stored in IndexedDB; the history is the CRDT's own log, so scrolling back through a month of edits is reading, not reconstructing. Sync between devices is optional and goes through a relay that only ever sees encrypted changes.

Where it stands

Version 2 shipped in September. The undo described in my October essay started here, before it moved to work.

2 October 2026 · 5 min read

Undo is a feature, not a stack

Every editor I have worked on started with the same undo: a stack of the last hundred changes, popped one at a time. It works until two people edit the same document, or one person edits it on two devices - then the stack is a lie about whose change comes next.

- Noor
